title: Mask Adoption Dynamics Simulation
description: Simulate how individuals adopt mask-wearing over time under social influence, information exposure, policy mandates, and supply constraints.

interactions.name: social_influence_on_adoption
interactions.description: People update mask attitudes and behavior based on the adoption of their social contacts.

interactions.name: visit_and_contact_at_location
interactions.description: People visit locations, generate contacts, and may face enforcement of mask rules.

interactions.name: policy_enforcement
interactions.description: Locations or authorities enforce mask requirements, affecting compliance probabilities.

interactions.name: mask_purchase
interactions.description: People attempt to buy masks; success depends on inventory, price, and access.

interactions.name: information_diffusion
interactions.description: Media and information sources broadcast messages that shift risk perception and attitudes.

interactions.name: policy_adjustment_feedback
interactions.description: PolicyMaker updates mandates and campaigns based on observed adoption or external triggers.

metrics.name: adoption_rate_over_time
metrics.description: Fraction of people wearing a mask at each time step.

metrics.name: time_to_50_percent_adoption
metrics.description: Number of days until the population reaches 50% mask adoption.

metrics.name: peak_adoption_rate
metrics.description: Maximum observed adoption rate during the simulation.

metrics.name: average_compliance_in_contacts
metrics.description: Share of person-to-person contacts where both parties are masked.

metrics.name: adoption_by_group
metrics.description: Adoption rates stratified by age group, SES, or region.

metrics.name: policy_effect_size
metrics.description: Change in adoption rate attributable to policy (e.g., difference-in-differences pre vs post mandate).

metrics.name: supply_shortage_days
metrics.description: Number of days when demand for masks exceeds available inventory.

metrics.name: adoption_inequality_index
metrics.description: Inequality of adoption across groups (e.g., Gini or Theil index).

validation_criteria.name: monotonic_policy_response
validation_criteria.description: On average, stronger policy strength should not reduce adoption compared to weaker policy in sensitivity tests.

validation_criteria.name: steady_state_stability
validation_criteria.description: In the final 14 days, the absolute daily change in adoption rate stays below 0.5% for at least 10 days.

validation_criteria.name: stochastic_convergence
validation_criteria.description: Across at least 30 Monte Carlo runs, the standard deviation of final-day adoption is below 5 percentage points.

validation_criteria.name: empirical_fit_optional
validation_criteria.description: If an empirical adoption time series is provided, RMSE between simulated and observed adoption is below a predefined threshold.
